requirements.evidence: Both migrations match the spec: names, FKs with cascadeOnDelete, role default 'employee', storedAs owner_seq and the named unique indexes (create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-28, create_entities_table.php:19-26). The contract is fully present: Entity::getRouteKeyName/memberships/users/owner (Entity.php:26-56), membership scopes, cast and relations (EntityMembership.php:86-131), UserRole::manageable (UserRole.php:15-18), User::memberships/entities/membershipFor (User.php:153-172), factories with owner/admin/employee states, and both policies with the exact rules, including owner-membership delete protection and self-removal (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:26-37). docs/database-schema.md drops owner_membership_id as the task asks.

conventions.evidence: Authorization is done in policies under app/Policies, mass assignment is set deliberately with #[Fillable] the same way as User, factories follow sibling style, down() is reversible and docs/database-schema.md is updated. Deviations: the migration timestamps 2026_10_29_000000/000001 suggest they were hand-written rather than made with make:migration, CHANGELOG.md has no [Unreleased] entry, and User::membershipFor (User.php:169) has no PHPDoc.

security.evidence: Policies deny non-members everywhere: membershipFor returns null, so the role check fails (EntityPolicy.php:271-295). The owner's membership can never be deleted (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:228). Ownership uniqueness is enforced in the database, not only in the app. Fillable is explicit. Adding 'role' to fillable is acceptable because writes will go through authorized actions. The task adds no routes or UI, so there is no input surface.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php covers: slug binding and soft deletes; the DB default role through a raw insert (lines 574-577); index names (604-609); a second owner rejected on both insert and promotion (611-621); multiple owners across entities and many non-owners (623-632); the duplicate-user unique and cascade (634-644); a full allow/deny matrix for both policies, including outsiders and cross-entity admins (646-705); and policy discovery through the Gate.

simplicity.evidence: The code is minimal and direct. It reuses membershipFor in both policies and has small private isOwnerOrAdmin helpers. The ownership constraint is a single generated column plus a unique index. There are no extra layers.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are short and typed with generic PHPDoc on relations, and the migration comment explains why NULLs don't collide (lines 441-442). There is no dead code.

scope.evidence: The diff touches only models, the enum, policies, factories, migrations, the schema doc and one test file. It adds no routes, middleware, session or UI.

issues.explanation: The conventions require a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry for this change, and the diff has none.
The zeroed time part of the timestamps suggests the migrations were hand-written rather than created with make:migration as the conventions require.
The new public method membershipFor has no PHPDoc, while the conventions ask for PHPDoc on public methods you touch.

The strict === comparison of user_id with getKey() relies on the driver returning integers. If the driver returns the ID as a string, self-removal would be silently denied; an int cast or $membership->user()->is($user) would be more robust.

review.summary: Adds the entities and entity_memberships tables (including the generated owner_seq column with a unique index that enforces one owner per entity in the database), the models, the enum, factories, both policies, an updated schema doc and thorough Pest tests covering every requirement and the full authorization matrix. It is correct, lean and well scoped; the only gaps are small convention nits (no CHANGELOG entry, migrations that look hand-written, one missing PHPDoc), so it would be approved with nits.
